summary: CrescentCare did a compliance-first review of Redwood's data residency and KMS options. Key asks: strict region pinning for EU PII, customer-managed KMS with double-wrap for egress, sub-processor disclosure for EU regions, and audit log retention options. Redwood clarified hosted vs dedicated behavior, fallback routing, and steps for an on-prem or VPC Private deployment. Agreed next steps include sending SOC2 + DPA and scheduling a focused technical demo for infra team.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-19 15:30 UTC
Duration: 44 minutes
Attendees: Priya Desai, Marco Ruiz, Jia Chen (Redwood) -- Amira Singh, Ben Taylor, Diego Ramos, Sofia Lee (CrescentCare)

[00:00] Priya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Amira: Amira here.
[00:07] Ben: Ben, hi.
[00:08] Diego: Diego, yep.
[00:10] Priya: Great. We're here to go through the data residency stuff, KMS, sub-processors, and any redlines you have in the DPA. Marco and Jia are going to handle the technical bits.

[00:25] Marco: Hi all. Quick agenda: region pinning behavior, what happens if capacity is constrained, KMS options (hosted vs customer-managed), audit logs, and sub-processor model.

[00:40] Ben: So the top requirement from our compliance team is strict region pinning for EU-sourced PII. We can't have EU data leave the EU unless there's an explicit legal basis. How does Redwood ensure requests from our EU app stay in EU?

[00:57] Marco: Good question. For hosted mode, we offer region affinity routing where requests are routed to EU clusters by default. There is an option—region pinning—that forces routing to EU-only endpoints. If a requested model variant isn't available in-region, Redwood can either fail the request or fallback to a compatible model in-region; unconditional cross-border fallback requires an explicit policy opt-in.

[01:24] Diego: What about automatic fallback? Do you do invisible fallback to US? That's a blocker for us.

[01:30] Jia: We do not silently cross-border EU data. Default behavior is to fail when region pinning is enabled. There is a configurable policy to permit fallback but it has to be enabled at customer level; it's off by default for customers with EU data residency needs.

[01:45] Ben: Ok, good. Second thing: KMS. We need customer-managed keys and ideally double-wrap with our HSM provider. Is that supported?

[01:53] Marco: For Private (VPC) or Dedicated, you can bring your own KMS. We support AWS KMS imports, GCP KMS, and HSM integrations via key-escrow patterns. Double-wrap is achievable: Redwood can perform envelope encryption where the data key is wrapped by your KMS and then by our service key; we can provide the configuration docs. For hosted customers we offer host-managed keys but with a KMS escrow option—still working through HSM escrow for hosted plans.

[02:25] Amira: If we use BYOK in Dedicated, do you store any plaintext keys?

[02:29] Jia: No plaintext key storage. The data key never leaves the HSM boundary unwrapped; Redwood holds ephemeral wrapped keys and rotates service keys per our rotation policy. We can walk you through the key lifecycle.

[02:40] Sofia: How is audit logging handled? We need per-request metadata, token usage, IP, and model version; retention for 7 years is requested by legal.

[02:52] Marco: We capture request-level metadata and model versioning in our audit logs. For Hosted we retain X days by default (configurable). For Dedicated/Private we can retain logs as long as required—there's an add-on for extended retention (long-term storage in customer's S3 or your logging provider). Seven years is operationally possible in Dedicated with an archived export pattern.

[03:20] Ben: Export to our S3 with SSE-KMS?

[03:23] Marco: Yep. We can push logs to your S3 and wrap with your KMS key. That meets your encryption-at-rest and control requirements.

[03:30] Amira: Sub-processors: we need a list of any third parties that will touch EU data, their locations, and whether they are covered by the DPA or a subprocess addendum.

[03:40] Priya: We maintain a sub-processor inventory; I'll share the latest export. For hosted EU clusters we use cloud providers in-region and a small set of telemetry vendors—everything's in the sub-processor list and covered by our DPA. If you need more granular attestation (per-region list), we can provide that.

[03:58] Ben: Are you using US-based analytics that process logs? That's a no-go unless anonymized.

[04:05] Priya: We can provide regionally isolated telemetry pipelines for enterprise customers. For CrescentCare, we can scope telemetry to EU-only. We'll mark that as an option in the DPA.

[04:18] Diego: On latency/capacity: if we enable strict pinning but spike traffic, is there a recommended rollout? We don't want 503s in production.

[04:26] Marco: Recommended pattern: start with region pinning plus a canary route that allows fallback for a small % to a secondary region while you validate. Alternatively, Dedicated capacity removes cross-region routing concerns since capacity is reserved in your chosen region. Autoscale policies for Dedicated can handle spikes without cross-border fallback.

[04:48] Amira: So for our timeline—Q4 rollout—we're leaning Dedicated in EU region. What's the onboarding lead time?

[04:55] Priya: Typical lead time for Dedicated is 6–8 weeks after contract, sometimes faster with existing capacity. For Private VPC/on-prem it'll be longer.

[05:05] Ben: DPA redlines: privacy team will send a few redlines around subprocessor notification periods and audit access. Can you accept a 30-day notification window?

[05:13] Priya: We usually do 45 days but we can discuss 30 for enterprise accounts; I'll flag for legal. We'll share the latest DPA and SOC2 link after this call.

[05:24] Sofia: Any difference in model catalog by region? E.g., some quantized variants might not be available in EU immediately.

[05:32] Marco: Right now model availability can vary. For certain optimized variants we do staged rollouts. That's why region pinning + fallback policy is important. For Dedicated you can pin the exact model version and we guarantee parity.

[05:47] Ben: Regarding SCCs and data transfer mechanisms—do you rely on standard contractual clauses or adequacy decisions?

[05:53] Priya: We rely on SCCs and, where available, we can use adequacy. For customers needing additional guarantees we support DPA clauses that reference SCCs and have an addendum for international transfers. We'll provide legal language.

[06:06] Amira: One more technical ask: can you annotate logs with the tenant id and the original region so our auditors can reconstruct flows?

[06:13] Marco: Yes, we can include tenant id, region, model id, request id, and latency metrics. We'll document the schema.

[06:22] Ben: For the customer-managed KMS, are you able to support key rotation triggered by our side and immediate revocation workflows? We need to ensure key compromise can be mitigated quickly.

[06:32] Jia: We support rotation events and revocation workflows. On revocation, tokens encrypted with the previous key are unusable; we recommend a rolling re-encrypt pattern where we rewrap a short-lived data key. We'll send the operational runbook for this.

[06:50] Diego: Request: can you provide a simple proof-of-concept where we push requests from our EU cloud to your EU endpoint and you stream logs to our S3? Diego: we can demo traffic and validate there's no cross-border egress.

[07:02] Marco: Absolutely. We can do a 2-week PoC with a scoped dataset and show logs, keys, and model outputs.

[07:10] Priya: Great. I'll attach SOC2 and DPA and set up Marco to run the PoC. Any other blockers?

[07:16] Amira: Not right now. Just need the legal docs and the subprocessor list per region.

[07:21] Ben: Also, please confirm retention and deletion workflows: when we request data deletion, how long until all logs and cached KVs are purged across backups?

[07:31] Marco: Deletion flows differ by deployment: Hosted has eventual deletion with snapshot windows and backup retention—typically 30–90 days for backups unless you choose the long-term export path. Dedicated/Private can enable immediate purge and we can coordinate retention windows. We'll include the retention SLA in the runbook.

[07:52] Priya: Ok quick recap: Priya will send SOC2 + DPA + sub-processor export; Marco will schedule a dedicated technical demo and prepare KMS/runbook docs; Diego will share infra diagram and target IP ranges. We'll aim to start PoC in early September.

[08:10] Sofia: Sounds good.
[08:12] Amira: Thanks everyone.

[08:15] Priya: Thanks, bye.

End of recording.

Notes on transcription quality: a few proper nouns may be off (KV cache sometimes transcribed as K V cash), occasional filler words removed for readability.
